messages:
maria: ran a seq/batch sweep on L40S (build r2) focused on attention kernels — wanted to check paged-evict behavior under kv cache pressure. results look odd, dropping throughput when spill starts. attaching quick numbers below.

maria: quick summary table (tokens/sec) from the run: 
```
HW  | Variant        | seq | batch | tok/s
L40S| fused          | 2048| 8     | 110k
L40S| paged-nop      | 2048| 8     | 105k
L40S| paged-evict    | 2048| 8     | 85k   <-- regression ~22% vs fused
L40S| paged-evict    | 512 | 16    | 120k
L40S| fused          | 512 | 16    | 125k
```
NOTE: at seq=2048 the paged-evict variant starts doing KV-cache spills > 1.2GB which seems correlated with the drop.

ben: ouch. did you run same on H100/A100?

maria: repro on H100 but smaller (about 8-10% drop). A100 didn't show the drop in our quick run, though kernel choices were different (fallbacks).

liam: do we have profiler timeline? flame or nvtx?

maria: pasted a snippet from nvprof timeline: 
```
[time 0.00s] fused_attn_kernel (smem=48KB)  ->  34ms
[time 0.03s] paged_eviction_scan (smem=80KB) ->  68ms  (stalls, memcopy to pager)
[time 0.10s] kv_spill_copy -> 120ms (device->host?)
```
looks like paged-evict triggers extra host-device copies when spill threshold reached.

aj: is that host staging or peer-to-peer? could be our cpu-side pager thread saturating. which allocator path is used?

maria: build r2 uses the new jemalloc slab + pager thread. the copy path shows pinned-buffer transfers. I can attach the full nvprof later.

liam: kernel selection maybe choosing a kernel that expects in-GPU contiguous K/V but paged layout forces scatter/gather; fallback uses a less-optimized kernel for that pattern. can you share kernel selection logs?

maria: yes, attached excerpt: 
```
[kernel-decider] seq=2048,batch=8 -> attempt: fused_fast (fails memcheck) -> fallback: paged_eviction_scan
[kernel-decider] paged_eviction_scan -> uses scatter-gather path, enables host-staging on >1GB spill
```

bench-bot: summary posted to #bench-logs: run 1851003333, L40S, paged-evict regress -22% @ seq=2048 bsz=8.

ben: can we reproduce with smaller model or synthetic? helps isolate kernel vs model layout.

maria: repro with synthetic seq patterns and dummy KV shows same pattern. attaching command: 
```
./bench --model tiny --hw l40s --variant paged-evict --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kv-fill 1.3GB
```

liam: next steps I suggest: 1) capture cprofile / nvtx full timeline, 2) collect kernel selection trace for that run, 3) try forcing fused kernel with patched mem layout to see if we can avoid fallback, 4) create an issue and tag runtime-kernels.

maria: opening issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1284 (WIP) — pinging @eng-runtime and @eng-runtime-infra.

aj: I'll allocate a small debug node with extra tracing (pcie counters) and try to reproduce. I'll post node id and ssh.

maria: thanks. for tracking: labeling as P1 perf-regression when kv spills. prioritizing since this affects Dedicated customers with long context workloads.

liam: also check the kernel's shared-mem usage heuristics — we may need a different threshold for L40S vs H100. last time we tuned those heuristics they were H100-biased.

ben: small ask: include a minimal reproducer (repo snippet) in the issue so infra can run quickly.

maria: will do. adding reproducer and nvprof tarball. thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: allocated debug node 'l40s-debug-07' (ip 10.12.8.7). expires in 6h.

aj: grabbing it now. will post logs in this thread once done.

maria: ack, leaving notes in the issue with timeline + next steps.

bench-bot: note: baseline fused vs paged-evict numbers stored under /bench/results/1851003333.json

ben: great, keep us posted. if we confirm kernel-choice bug we should roll a micropatch to force fused for the short term while root cause is fixed.

liam: agreed. also schedule a short sync tomorrow if needed.

maria: thanks everyone.
